transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you could make it in today. What brings you in to see me?

Hi. Well, I came in because... I just can't get my head to stay quiet. I drive a taxi, and even when I know for a fact I did my safety check on the cab, this thought just keeps hitting me that I missed something. Like I missed a step and somebody could get hurt, or my boss is gonna say I lied about doing the check in the first place. 

I just... I can't make the thought shut up. It doesn't matter if I'm out driving or if I'm just trying to study, it's always there.
When that thought comes up, do you find yourself going back to re-check the cab or doing something specific to ease that worry?

Yeah, I do. Before I can take a ride, I... I keep going around the car. I check the tires, the lights, the doors, the meter, all the paperwork, just over and over again. Sometimes I even take pictures of it all, and if it just doesn't feel right, I have to restart the whole check from the beginning. It's... it's bad. I'll do it even when passengers are standing right there waiting for me and I'm already late. I just have to be sure.
How long have you been dealing with these intrusive thoughts and repetitive checking routines?

I'm not really sure exactly when it started. It feels like it's been going on for a while now, but I can't put an exact date on it. It just kind of became a part of my routine at some point, and now it's just... always there.
